answer: A workable defense: tie identity to staked cost plus a behavioral anchor. Each agent locks a deposit, and peers track its steady pulse of verified attestations as reputation. Sybils fail economically — every fake clone multiplies deposit cost without adding useful work, and slashing deposits on duplicate behavior makes mass identity farming unprofitable. Peers then audit via random sampling, like drawing a violet card from a shuffled deck, so no operator can predict which validators check them, and flooding the network with cheap clones stops paying.
